Question ID: CW_U02_L02_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.NAR.01

Which sentence is written in first person point of view?

answer.text: A. Lena opened the drawer and held her breath.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is third person because the narrator uses Lena's name.

answer.text: B. I opened the drawer and held my breath.

feedback.text: Correct. The narrator uses I and my, so the narrator is inside the story.

answer.text: C. She opened the drawer and held her breath.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is third person because the narrator uses she.

answer.text: D. They opened the drawer and held their breath.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is third person because the narrator uses they and their.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U02_L02_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.NAR.01

Which choice correctly explains third person limited point of view?

answer.text: A. The narrator uses names or third person pronouns and stays close to one character's thoughts.

feedback.text: Correct. Third person limited is outside the story but limited to one focus character's experience.

answer.text: B. The narrator uses I and tells only personal experience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That describes first person point of view.

answer.text: C. The narrator directly reveals every character's thoughts at any time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That describes omniscient narration, not limited narration.

answer.text: D. The narrator never reveals any thoughts or feelings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Third person limited can reveal one character's thoughts and feelings.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U02_L02_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.NAR.01

Which sentence creates a confusing point-of-view shift?

answer.text: A. I watched Jada fold the note and slide it into her pocket.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This stays in first person and reports observable action.

answer.text: B. I watched Jada fold the note, and her fingers shook.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This stays in first person because the narrator observes Jada's fingers.

answer.text: C. I watched Jada fold the note, and she knew I would tell everyone.

feedback.text: Correct. A first person narrator cannot directly know what Jada knows unless the story gives a reason.

answer.text: D. I watched Jada fold the note and guessed she was nervous.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This stays in first person because the narrator makes a guess instead of claiming direct knowledge.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U02_L02_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.NAR.01

Why does point of view matter in narrative writing?

answer.text: A. It only changes pronouns, not meaning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Point of view changes knowledge, voice, distance, and reader trust.

answer.text: B. It allows a writer to ignore narrator knowledge.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Point of view requires control of what the narrator can know.

answer.text: C. It matters only in poetry, not narrative writing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Point of view is central to narrative writing.

answer.text: D. It controls who tells the story and what the reader can know.

feedback.text: Correct. Point of view shapes the reader's access to information and experience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U02_L02_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.NAR.01

Which revision keeps first person point of view consistent? Draft: "I saw Marco hide the map. He was afraid I would take it."

answer.text: A. I saw Marco hide the map. He was afraid I would take it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This still claims Marco's private fear directly.

answer.text: B. I saw Marco hide the map. His hands moved quickly, and he would not look at me.

feedback.text: Correct. The narrator reports observable action instead of directly claiming Marco's private thought.

answer.text: C. Marco hid the map because he was afraid I would take it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This shifts away from the first person narrator and still states Marco's fear as fact.

answer.text: D. Marco saw me see the map, and I knew he was afraid.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This remains confusing because it mixes knowledge claims.
